title: The iPhone Duo Is Getting a Limited Version of Face ID
gist: Apple's iOS 27.3 adds a limited facial recognition unlock to the iPhone Duo foldable, borrowed from the HomeView smart display's Secure Exclave-based person recognition because the Duo lacks room for a TrueDepth sensor; it cannot authorize payments, needs recent Touch ID/passcode within 45 minutes, and signals how much Touch ID friction bothers Duo owners.

insights.claim: Apple's iPhone Duo foldable, its most expensive smartphone, lacks Face ID because the hinge and multiple display layers leave no room for the TrueDepth sensor, so it relies on Touch ID.
insights.speaker: Julian Chokkattu
insights.so_what: Foldable form factors force component trade-offs, constraining Apple's feature parity across its premium lineup.
insights.locator: Apple's most expensive smartphone—the iPhone Duo

insights.claim: Rumors say Apple is racing to add full Face ID to the second-generation iPhone Duo, but tight development cycles may push it to the third generation in 2028.
insights.speaker: Julian Chokkattu
insights.so_what: Timeline for full biometric parity on Apple's foldable informs upgrade-cycle expectations for the Duo line.
insights.locator: Rumors abound that Apple is racing

insights.claim: iOS 27.3 brings facial recognition to the iPhone Duo by borrowing the person-recognition technology from Apple's HomeView smart display, protected by the Secure Exclave memory-protected space in the A20 Pro processor rather than the Secure Enclave used for Face ID.
insights.speaker: Julian Chokkattu
insights.so_what: Apple is reusing software and silicon features across device categories to patch hardware gaps.
insights.locator: That's changing now in a software update

insights.claim: The iPhone Duo's new face recognition cannot authenticate payments or sensitive apps, requires a Touch ID or passcode authentication within the past 45 minutes, and works only on the front screen when the phone is folded.
insights.speaker: Julian Chokkattu
insights.so_what: The feature is convenience-only, not a security replacement, limiting its value versus true Face ID.
insights.locator: You cannot use it to authenticate payments

insights.claim: Apple's willingness to ship a watered-down Face ID is a rare compromise for the company and shows how much of a friction point Touch ID has become for iPhone Duo owners.
insights.speaker: Julian Chokkattu
insights.so_what: Signals user-experience pain on Apple's first foldable that Apple is prioritizing; relevant for Duo satisfaction and next-gen design.
insights.quote: Apple’s willingness to roll out a watered-down version of Face ID is a rare compromise for the company

insights.claim: Google's newer Pixel folding phones are the only foldables on the US market with secure facial authentication, though weaker in the dark than Face ID, while Samsung's Galaxy facial biometrics are not strong enough to protect sensitive content.
insights.speaker: Julian Chokkattu
insights.so_what: Secure face unlock is a competitive differentiator in foldables where Google currently leads Apple and Samsung.
